# Scholtz — Algorithms for Mapping Diatonic Keyboard Tunings and Temperaments (1998)

## Chicago 18 forms

**Full note:** Kenneth P. Scholtz, “Algorithms for Mapping Diatonic Keyboard Tunings and Temperaments,” *Music Theory Online* 4, no. 4 (July 1998), §§3.1–4.1, https://www.mtosmt.org/issues/mto.98.4.4/mto.98.4.4.scholtz.html.

**Shortened note:** Scholtz, “Algorithms for Mapping.”

**Bibliography:** Scholtz, Kenneth P. “Algorithms for Mapping Diatonic Keyboard Tunings and Temperaments.” *Music Theory Online* 4, no. 4 (July 1998). https://www.mtosmt.org/issues/mto.98.4.4/mto.98.4.4.scholtz.html.

## Essay use

Scholtz fixes ratios within a Pythagorean keyboard-tuning construction: fifth \(3/2\), fourth \(4/3\), octave \(2/1\), and a \(9/8\) major-tone construction. The Pythagorean comma and equal-temperament adjustment provide the needed constraint: pure-fifth chains do not simply produce a literal unadjusted octave return.

**Claim boundary:** the article establishes relations among specified historical tuning systems. It does not establish Spanda, QL, toroidal topology, metaphysical return, or a general claim about every whole tone/equal temperament.

<a id="scholtz-1998-algorithms-diatonic-keyboard-tunings-q001"></a>
## Passage card — `scholtz-1998-algorithms-diatonic-keyboard-tunings-q001` — Pythagorean ratio chain
^scholtz-1998-algorithms-diatonic-keyboard-tunings-q001

> “The links are a sequence of powers of 3/2 to the right of C and powers of 4/3 to the left of C. Whenever necessary, the fraction is divided by two to keep the pitch within the compass of a single 2/1 octave. Thus, 3/2 x 3/2 = 9/4. 9/4 is divided by 2, making D = 9/8.”

- **Locator:** §3.1; official HTML; official PDF viewer p. 3/15 (PDF index 2).

<a id="scholtz-1998-algorithms-diatonic-keyboard-tunings-q002"></a>
## Passage card — `scholtz-1998-algorithms-diatonic-keyboard-tunings-q002` — Pythagorean comma
^scholtz-1998-algorithms-diatonic-keyboard-tunings-q002

> “Although D♯ (19683/16384) and E♭ (32/27) are enharmonically identical in equal temperament, their pitches in Pythagorean tuning are different; D♯ is higher than E♭ by 531441/524288—the Pythagorean comma (P). The more common method for deriving the Pythagorean comma is to calculate it as the difference between 12 consecutive fifths and seven octaves.”

- **Locator:** §3.2; official HTML; official PDF viewer p. 3/15 (PDF index 2).
- **Status:** quotation-ready.
- **Verification:** Luna acquisition agent and coordinator, 2026-07-14; manually transcribed from official HTML and checked against publisher PDF; OCR uncertainty: none.
- **Source relation:** extracted.
- **Evidential action:** qualifies.
- **Argument function:** technical limitation.
- **Consumers:** [[26-s3-p1-spanda-4-2]]; [[29-s3-p4-topology-music-resolution]]; [Core Theorem Bridge](../../../../../eight-determinations.md); [[section-rooms/arguments/A16-Arche-Topos-as-Differential-Field|Arche-Topos as Differential Field]]; movements 26/29 comma boundary.
- **Use boundary:** prevents treating pure fifth iteration as a simple exact octave return; it does not turn the comma into evidence for QL or topological return.

<a id="scholtz-1998-algorithms-diatonic-keyboard-tunings-q003"></a>
## Passage card — `scholtz-1998-algorithms-diatonic-keyboard-tunings-q003` — temperament adjustment
^scholtz-1998-algorithms-diatonic-keyboard-tunings-q003

> “Equal temperament flattens the fifths (and sharpens the fourths) by 1/12 of a Pythagorean comma… This is just enough to give a true octave from a chain of 12 links. In musical terms, the 12 fifths in the chromatic line are made exactly equal to 7 octaves.”

- **Locator:** §4.1; official HTML; official PDF viewer p. 4/15 (PDF index 3).
- **Status:** quotation-ready.
- **Verification:** Luna acquisition agent and coordinator, 2026-07-14; manually transcribed from official HTML and checked against publisher PDF; OCR uncertainty: none.
- **Source relation:** extracted.
- **Evidential action:** qualifies.
- **Argument function:** historical/technical counterposition.
- **Consumers:** [[26-s3-p1-spanda-4-2]]; [[29-s3-p4-topology-music-resolution]]; [Core Theorem Bridge](../../../../../eight-determinations.md); [[section-rooms/arguments/A16-Arche-Topos-as-Differential-Field|Arche-Topos as Differential Field]]; movement 29 tuning-system limitation.
- **Use boundary:** describes a temperament-specific adjustment; it does not make an equal-tempered octave an unaltered consequence of pure \(3/2\) fifths or a QL theorem.
